title: Tracing How yield Pauses and Resumes a Generator Lexer
description: Step through a generator function that yields tokens one at a time as next(gen) advances and pauses execution.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `tokens(source)` contains `yield m.group()` on line 8, which makes `tokens` a generator function. Inside the `re.finditer(r"\w+", source)` loop, line 7 prints before `yield` pauses the frame, and line 9 prints `resumed` when the caller asks for the next item.
Line 13 calls `gen = tokens("let x")`, line 14 prints `"gen exists"`, and line 15 calls `next(gen)` for the first time.

steps.question: Does `"  started"` (line 5) print during `gen = tokens("let x")` on line 13, or after `"gen exists"` when `next(gen)` runs on line 15?
steps.answer: It prints after `"gen exists"`. Calling `tokens("let x")` on line 13 creates the suspended generator object `gen` without running line 5. The first `next(gen)` call on line 15 starts the body up to the first `yield` on line 8.

steps.description: Line 16 calls `next(gen)` a second time (resuming at line 9, yielding `'x'`, and pausing at line 8 again). On line 18, the third `next(gen)` resumes at line 9, finishes the loop, prints `"  finished"` on line 10, and raises `StopIteration`, which lines 19-20 catch.
At trace step 7, after line 14 has already printed `gen exists` and line 15 has called `next(gen)`, execution enters `tokens` at line 5 for the first time.
